privacy.title: KVKK privacy notice
privacy.draft: Draft — requires approval by legal counsel
privacy.intro: Some records and reports in ARCILOGGER contain personal data. Please read this before you continue.

body.data: These reports contain personal data: IP and MAC addresses, device names, person and department information and internet usage records. Usage times are estimates, not exact screen time.
body.purpose: This data is processed to support the obligations under Law No. 5651 and to keep the company network secure; it must not be used for any other purpose.
body.access: Access personal data only as far as your duties require. Do not share it with unauthorised people and keep exported files safe.
body.audit: Views and exports of personal data, and your acceptance of this notice, are written to the audit log.
body.storage: The data is kept on the company's own server, is not transferred abroad and is destroyed at the end of the retention period. See the company's privacy notice and retention and deletion policy for details.

privacy.readConfirm: I have read and understood this notice.

setup.title: Initial setup
setup.doneNotice: The administrator account was created. Sign in now; two-factor authentication is set up at the first sign-in.
setup.noTokenBody: Run the command below on the server console; the one-time token it prints is valid for 24 hours.
setup.tokenHint: The token printed by 'arcilogger-api setup-token'. It works only once.

forbidden.title: You do not have permission for this page

users.title: Users and roles

users.tempDescription: Temporary password for {{name}} ({{username}}). Pass it to the user over a safe channel.
users.tempOnce: This password is shown only once. The user must change it at the first sign-in.

deactivate.title: Disable user
deactivate.body: {{name}} ({{username}}) can no longer sign in and their open sessions are closed. Their records and audit history are kept.

resetPassword.title: Reset password
resetPassword.body: A new temporary password is created for {{name}} ({{username}}); the old password stops working, open sessions are closed and the account is unlocked.

resetTotp.body: The authenticator link and the recovery codes of {{name}} ({{username}}) are deleted; the user sets them up again at the next sign-in. Only do this for a user whose identity you have verified (e.g. lost phone).

unlock.title: Unlock account
unlock.body: The lock of {{name}} ({{username}}) is removed and the failed-attempt counter is reset.

errors.order: The last day cannot be before the first day.

audit.description: A tamper-evident record of every action in ARCILOGGER. Entries are chained with SHA-256 hashes and sealed every night.
audit.caption: Audit log, newest entry first
audit.empty: No entries match these filters. Try a wider time range.
audit.end: You reached the beginning of the log.

chain.brokenTitle: The audit log chain does not verify
chain.brokenBody: The hash or the chain link of one or more entries does not match. Entries may have been changed or deleted; inform the system administrator and the auditor at once.

detail.subtitle: Entry #{{id}}
detail.formula: Hash = SHA-256(hash of the previous entry + the canonical entry below, RFC 8785).
detail.match: Hash recomputed in this browser: matches
detail.mismatch: Hash does not match: the entry may have been changed
detail.noCrypto: The hash could not be computed in this browser (a secure connection is required)
detail.notCanonical: The hash could not be computed in this browser
detail.masked: The target is shown by its pseudonym: the hash cannot be recomputed in this browser
detail.hidden: Hashes are not shown to readers who see pseudonyms: the chain is verified on the server
detail.maskedTarget: You see pseudonyms on the usage pages, so the target is the person's or device's pseudonym token (the key of the usage pages, e.g. d:ad36… for Cihaz-AD36). The entry was not changed. Its hash covers the real target, so the hashes are not shown to you (a guess could be tested against them); the chain verification checks the whole log on the server.

download.match: The downloaded file's hash was recomputed in this browser: it matches
download.mismatch: The downloaded file's hash does not match: do not use the file, download it again

unchecked.no-crypto: The hash cannot be computed in this browser (a secure connection is needed)
unchecked.too-large: The file is too large to hash in the browser; use the verifier in the package
unchecked.no-hash: The server announced no hash for this file

raw.title: Raw log line
raw.subtitle: {{source}} · {{day}} · line {{line}}
raw.text: Line (as stored; invisible characters shown as escapes)
raw.escapes: Escapes such as #012 are the file's own; \xNN marks a byte that is not UTF-8, \uXXXX an invisible or direction-changing character.
raw.sha256: SHA-256 of the line (without its line feed)
raw.audited: This view was recorded in the audit log (with the line's position and hash, not its content).

lookup.description: Finds the session and the device/person behind an address, port and time of an official request, with the evidence of every step. Designed to support 5651 obligations; ask your legal counsel how results are handed over.
lookup.emptyTitle: Enter the request details and the query
lookup.emptyBody: Results, the matching sessions and the evidence of every step appear here.

form.label: 5651 lookup
form.requestHint: All required; results are shown only after the request details were entered.
form.authorityHint: E.g. Izmir Chief Public Prosecutor's Office
form.reasonHint: Subject and basis of the request; line breaks allowed.
form.queryHint: At least one of public/WAN IP, internal IP, MAC, destination IP or domain is needed.
form.timeHint: 24 hours, e.g. 14:05:30 — the time of the request, in the time zone below.
form.timeZoneHint: Default: Europe/Istanbul (UTC+03:00). Choose UTC if the request gives UTC.
form.destinationHint: A destination narrows the candidate list caused by double NAT considerably.
form.internalHint: With an internal IP or MAC the IP-MAC-device-person chain is shown directly.
form.auditNote: The lookup and the request details are recorded in the audit log (the reason only as a hash).

validation.futureRequest: The request date cannot be after today.
validation.ip: Enter a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.
validation.ipv6: This version does not support 5651 lookups for IPv6 addresses: ARCILOGGER does not collect the records that tie IPv6 addresses to devices (NDP, DHCPv6). The request must be answered by other means. Enter an IPv4 address written as IPv6 (::ffff:…) as IPv4.
validation.port: The port must be a number from 0 to 65535.
validation.domain: Enter a valid domain name (no spaces, /, \, @ or :).
validation.mac: A MAC address has 12 hexadecimal digits (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff).
validation.time: Enter the time as HH:MM or HH:MM:ss.
validation.timeZone: Choose a time zone from the list.
validation.tolerance: The tolerance must be from 0 to {{max}} seconds.
validation.target: Enter at least one of public/WAN IP, internal IP, MAC, destination IP or domain.

conflict.body: This IP address was held by more than one MAC address at this moment. No single device or person can be named with certainty; every possible chain is listed below with the same weight.

result.title: Lookup #{{id}}
result.noneBody: The explanations above say why and which data would make the answer exact.
result.truncatedNote: The list was shortened; add destination details or narrow the tolerance and look up again.

window.text: Requested day {{day}} · in the database: {{database}} · in the sealed vault: {{vault}} · database records: {{range}}

match.title: #{{rank}}
match.noChain: No attribution chain could be built for this session's source address.

destinationMatch.domain_address: Only the address matched: the domain was not seen for this client; the address is known from another client's logs (may be a shared CDN address)
destinationMatch.domain_unverified: Destination not verified: the NAT address and port identify the session, but no log ties it to the requested domain

report.title: Official report and evidence package
report.note: The report is generated and stored on the first download; every later download gives the same file. Every download is recorded in the audit log.
report.hashHint: Write this hash into the hand-over record; it shows that the report was not changed.

timestamp.notRequested: No time stamp was requested for the report (Settings: lookup.report_timestamp off).
timestamp.failedTitle: The report could not be time-stamped
timestamp.notLegal: The report hash was stamped by the provider {{provider}}; it is not the Kamu SM production server, so the stamp has no legal validity. For trials only.

history.allUsers: Every user's lookups (administrator view). A row opens that lookup's results; every opening is recorded in the audit log.
history.ownOnly: Only your own lookups. A row opens that lookup's results.
history.caption: Earlier 5651 lookups, newest first

evidence.description: ZIP packages of sealed days for official requests, each with its own verifier. Creating a package and every download are recorded in the audit log.
evidence.readOnly: You can view and download packages; creating them is for administrators.
evidence.caption: Evidence packages, newest first
evidence.requested: Package requested; it is being built in the background.

detail.title: Package #{{id}}
detail.building: The package is being built; this section refreshes itself every few seconds.
detail.failedTitle: The package could not be built
detail.gone: The package expired and its file was deleted. The evidence stays in the vault; create the package again if needed.
detail.notLegal: The time stamps of the days in this package come from a provider without legal validity (test/mock); the package is for trials only.
detail.rootUnconfirmed: The days of this package claim Kamu SM production time stamps, which verified; they are not shown as legally valid because not every root certificate's fingerprint is listed in tsa.legal_root_fingerprints. The package guide says which root fingerprint to compare with the value Kamu SM publishes.
detail.passwordYes: Yes (AES-256) — the password was shown once, when the package was created
detail.verifierHint: Write this value into the hand-over record and give it to the recipient apart from the package (phone, separate e-mail, by hand). The recipient checks with it that the package's verify.py was not changed (auditor guide, section 5).
detail.expiredUnpurged: The retention period of the package ended at {{time}}; it cannot be downloaded any more. Its file is deleted by the clean-up job that runs every night after 03:00. The evidence stays in the vault; create the package again if needed.

wizard.title: New evidence package
wizard.description: The package is built in the background and is only handed out after ARCILOGGER's own verifier passed it. Only sealed days can be packaged.
wizard.fromLookupHint: The raw lines the lookup result cites (other devices of an IP conflict included) and the lookup day.
wizard.fromRangeHint: The chosen days (at most {{max}}) and sources.
wizard.sourcesKnown: Separate with commas. Sealed sources of this day: {{sources}}
wizard.referenceLookupHint: Empty: the lookup's authority and file number are used.
wizard.fullDaysHint: All sealed files of the chosen sources on those days; the cited lines also under extract/.
wizard.extractHint: Only the lines you list below plus the complete sealed files of their sources on those days (the extract is checked byte by byte against the full file).
wizard.extractLookupHint: Only the lines the lookup result cites plus the complete sealed files of their sources on those days.
wizard.linesHint: One per line: day source line_number (e.g. 2026-10-09 fortigate 17).
wizard.passwordLabel: Protect the package with a password (AES-256)
wizard.passwordHint: The server generates the password and shows it only once, when the package is created; it is not stored anywhere. Without it the package cannot be opened — create it again. Give the password to the recipient apart from the package.
wizard.summaryNote: Creating needs a password confirmation within the last {{minutes}} minutes; you are asked if necessary. The number of packages built at the same time and the free space on the data disk are limited.
wizard.passwordYes: Yes (AES-256) — the password will be shown once, when the package is created
wizard.allSourcesHint: When ticked, the sealed file of every device that sent logs on those days goes into the package. Untick it to hand over only the sources the request needs (KVKK: data minimisation).
wizard.allSourcesLookupHint: For full days, when ticked, the sealed file of every device that sent logs on the lookup's days (e.g. all switches and access points) goes into the package — not only those of the sources the lookup cites. Untick it and choose the sources to avoid handing over more data than needed; the sources of the cited lines are always added. Not used for an extract.
wizard.sourcesLookupHint: Separate with commas (e.g. fortigate). The sources of the cited lines are added as well.
wizard.fullDaysLookupHint: On the days the lookup cites and the lookup day, all sealed files of the chosen sources — of every device that sent logs if "All sources" is ticked; the cited lines also under extract/.
wizard.sourcesAll: All sources — the sealed file of every device that sent logs on those days
wizard.sourcesLookupAll: All sources — the sealed file of every device that sent logs on those days (not only those of the sources the lookup cites)
wizard.sourcesLookupChosen: {{sources}} plus the sources of the lines the lookup cites
wizard.sourcesFromLookupLines: sources of the lines the lookup cites
wizard.auditLogLabel: Add the ARCILOGGER audit log (internal audits only)
wizard.auditLogHint: Off (recommended): the package does not contain the days' ARCILOGGER audit log (user names, IP addresses, lookups made); paket.json lists that file as "not included" with the reason and the verifier does not count it as a failure. Do not turn it on for a package handed to an authority (KVKK: data minimisation).
wizard.auditLogYes: Included — the days' ARCILOGGER audit log (internal audit)
wizard.auditLogNo: Not included (listed with the reason in paket.json)

password.title: Package password
password.onceTitle: This password is shown only now
password.onceBody: Write the password down and give it to the recipient apart from the package; without it the package cannot be opened.
password.label: Password
password.saved: I saved the password in a safe place.

validation.notClosed: Only finished (sealed) days can be chosen.
validation.order: The last day cannot be before the first day.
validation.tooManyDays: A package can hold at most {{max}} days.
validation.sourcesRequired: Enter at least one source or choose all sources.
validation.sourceName: Source names consist of lower-case letters, digits, dots and dashes (e.g. fortigate).
validation.linesFormat: Every line must read "day source line_number" (e.g. 2026-10-09 fortigate 17).
validation.linesRequired: Enter at least one line for an extract.
validation.tooManyLines: An extract can hold at most 10,000 lines.
validation.lineOutside: Cited lines must lie within the chosen days.

blocked.unfinished: The package can be downloaded once it is ready.
blocked.failed: A package that could not be built cannot be downloaded.
blocked.expired: The retention period is over; the package cannot be downloaded.
blocked.deleted: The package file is missing; the package cannot be downloaded.

evidence.largeHint: Large package ({{size}}): the browser receives the whole file before saving it; keep this page open until the download has finished. At this size the browser does not check the hash of the downloaded file (the recipient checks the package with the verifier inside it). If the browser runs out of memory or disk space, create the package again with fewer days or sources.

sealing.description: Every day is sealed at night: its files are compressed, hashed with SHA-256, chained to the previous day, and the daily manifest is time-stamped by Kamu SM.
sealing.providerNotLegal: The configured time-stamp provider ({{provider}}) is not the Kamu SM production server: its stamps have no legal validity. Production must use the Kamu SM production server only.
sealing.verifiedWindow: Green: sealed and verified within the last {{days}} days.
sealing.noDayTitle: Choose a day in the calendar
sealing.noDayBody: The files, manifest, time stamp and verification result of the chosen day appear here.

credits.title: Credit (Kamu SM)
credits.lowBody: The remaining credit ({{remaining}}) is below the alert threshold ({{threshold}}). Buy credit on the Kamu SM portal.
credits.unreadable_one: {{count}} line of the credit history could not be read.
credits.unreadable_other: {{count}} lines of the credit history could not be read.
credits.note: The \ARCILOGGER\Credit task queries the credit once a day; "Query credit" runs the task on the server once, now. The web service never connects to Kamu SM itself.
credits.queryLow: Credit left {{credits}}: below the alert threshold ({{threshold}}).

day.title: {{day}}
day.notLegal: This day's time stamp was issued by the provider {{provider}} and has no legal validity (test/mock). In production only stamps of the Kamu SM production server are valid.
day.rootUnconfirmed: This day's manifest says its time stamp comes from the Kamu SM production server ({{provider}}). The day is not shown as legally valid because the root certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint is not listed in tsa.legal_root_fingerprints, or the stamp did not verify. Compare the root's fingerprint with the value Kamu SM publishes.

verify.deep: Deep check (files are decompressed and hashed again)
verify.wait: The check runs in a separate process on the server and can take up to 5 minutes.

verification.title: Last verification
verification.none: No verification of this day recorded.
verification.inconclusive: The last check by hand was inconclusive ({{time}}, {{outcome}}).

sealNow.explanation: Seal now is not available from the web interface in this version: the web service may not write to the vault. Sealing runs as the scheduled task \ARCILOGGER\Seal every 5 minutes from 00:10 and retries failed attempts by itself. To seal at once, run that task in Task Scheduler on the server.
sealNow.hint: The sealing task tries this day once without waiting for its retry time; the wait after midnight, the empty-day rule and the order of days still apply.

blocked.open: The day has not ended yet; it is sealed after it ends.
blocked.notApplicable: This day is not sealed (no data, skipped or deleted).
blocked.notOldest: Only the next (oldest) unsealed day can be sealed now: {{day}} first.

sealNow.confirmBody: The \ARCILOGGER\Seal task on the server tries to seal this day once, now, with a time stamp from the configured provider (1 credit with Kamu SM). The wait after midnight and the empty-day rule are not skipped.

outcome.pending: {{day}} is not sealed yet; the task tries again later.
outcome.failed: The sealing attempt failed; the error is on the day page.
outcome.waiting: {{day}} is waiting; the task seals it later.
outcome.deleted: {{day}} was deleted after the retention period.

states.skipped: Empty day; not stamped on its own (listed in the next manifest)

chain.title: Chain
chain.matches: The chain link to the previous day ({{day}}) matches the files in the vault.
chain.broken: The chain link to the previous day ({{day}}) does NOT match: its manifest or time stamp may have been changed.
chain.unknown: The previous day ({{day}}) is not in the vault; the link could not be checked.
chain.start: This day is the first day of the chain (no link to a previous day).

reasons.none: no messages at all on this day
reasons.longer: no messages for more than {{minutes}} minutes

devices.description: Devices seen on the network, their owners and the assignment history the 5651 lookup relies on; persons, departments and the VLAN mapping. Every change is written to the audit log.
devices.readOnly: You can only view this page. Assigning and editing need the “Edit devices and persons” permission.
devices.caption: Devices seen on the network
devices.selectPage: Select every device on this page
devices.searchPlaceholder: MAC, host name, IP or device name
devices.emptyHint: Devices are not entered by hand: they are added as DHCP and ARP records are processed.

randomized.hint: Phones may change this address per network and over time.
randomized.title: Randomised (private) MAC address
randomized.titleSome_one: {{count}} device has a randomised MAC address
randomized.body: Phones and some laptops use a new random MAC address per network (and over time), so one phone can appear in the list as several devices. Assign each of them to the same person. The 5651 lookup uses the assignment, valid at the requested moment, of the MAC address seen then.

privacy.title: Waiting for the KVKK notice to be accepted
privacy.body: This section holds personal data (device owners' names). The list loads once you accept the notice shown.

detail.subtitle: Unnamed device
detail.infrastructureHint: Routers, switches, firewalls: not counted as IP conflicts and not listed as unknown devices.
detail.name: Device name
detail.nameHint: Shown in the 5651 chain, e.g. “Accounting printer”.
detail.noDepartmentVlan: None — the {{vlan}} VLAN has no department
detail.tagTooLong: A tag may have at most {{tag}} characters.

history.title: Assignment history
history.backfilled: taken over from the earlier record
history.appendOnly: The history is append-only: records are never corrected or deleted; a new assignment closes the previous one.

assign.descriptionAssign_one: {{count}} device is assigned to the person you choose. Its current assignment ends at the start time and stays in the history.
assign.descriptionAssign_other: {{count}} devices are assigned to the person you choose. Their current assignments end at the start time and stay in the history.
assign.descriptionUnassign_one: The current assignment of {{count}} device ends; the history is kept.
assign.descriptionUnassign_other: The current assignments of {{count}} devices end; the history is kept.
assign.morePersons: More persons match; narrow the search.

when.nowHint: From this moment (by the server's clock).
when.atHint: When the device was handed to this person earlier, e.g. a hand-over entered late.

assign.rules: The start cannot be in the future.
assign.rulesWithCurrent: The start can be neither in the future nor before the start of the selected devices' current assignment ({{time}}).
assign.noteHint: Optional; shown with the new assignment in the assignment history, e.g. the hand-over form number.
assign.doneUnassign_one: The assignment of {{count}} device was removed.
assign.doneUnassign_other: The assignments of {{count}} devices were removed.
assign.conflictHint: The start can be neither in the future nor before the device's current assignment began or its last one ended: the assignment history is append-only. Correct the time and try again; no device was changed.
assign.unchanged_one: {{count}} device was already in this state and was not changed.
assign.unchanged_other: {{count}} devices were already in this state and were not changed.

errors.noDevices: Select at least one device first.
errors.tooMany: At most 500 devices can be assigned at once.
errors.nothingToUnassign: None of the selected devices is assigned to a person.
errors.future: The start cannot be in the future.
errors.beforeCurrent: The start cannot be before the start of a selected device's current assignment.

persons.intro: Persons are never deleted: a deactivated person keeps the assignment history and the link in past 5651 results.
persons.caption: Persons
persons.searchPlaceholder: Name, e-mail, employee no. or title
persons.name: Full name
persons.title: Job title
persons.employeeNoHint: Used to find the person in a CSV import.
persons.keepsHistory: Inactive persons cannot be given devices; the assignment history is kept.
persons.usageExcludedHint: The person is not shown as a person on the usage pages and in usage reports; their traffic still counts in the company and department totals. 5651 lookups are not affected.
persons.formDescription: Only the name is required. Changes are written to the audit log.

confirmDeactivate.title: Deactivate the person
confirmDeactivate.body: {{name}} is not deleted: the assignment history and the link in past 5651 lookups are kept. An inactive person cannot be given devices. Devices assigned to this person now stay assigned; remove or move them on the Devices tab if needed.

persons.emptyHint: Add them one by one with “Add a person” or as a CSV file on the Import/Export tab.
persons.inactiveNote: This person is inactive: no devices can be assigned; the history is kept.
persons.usageExcludedNote: This person is excluded from usage reports: not shown as a person on the usage pages and in usage reports, while their traffic still counts in the company and department totals. 5651 lookups are not affected.
persons.noDevices: No device is assigned to this person now.

departments.title: Departments
departments.description: A device's department is that of its person; a device without a person takes its VLAN's department.
departments.caption: Departments
departments.name: Department name
departments.formDescription: The department name appears in the person list, the 5651 chain and reports. Changes are written to the audit log.
departments.emptyHint: Add the departments here; persons and VLANs are linked to them.

vlans.title: VLANs and subnets
vlans.description: Enter the organisation's VLANs and subnets here: devices take their VLAN's name, devices without a person also its department. A smaller network inside another one (e.g. a /25 inside a /24) comes first.
vlans.caption: VLANs
vlans.name: Name
vlans.empty: No VLANs yet: add your network
vlans.emptyHint: Add the VLANs and subnets one by one: the network address with its prefix length (e.g. 10.0.20.0/24), the VLAN id and a name. Collection, sealing, 5651 lookups and usage work without VLANs, but devices then get no VLAN name and no VLAN department.
vlans.emptyHintReadOnly: An administrator adds the VLANs; they appear here once added.
vlans.formDescription: Only the network and the name are required. Changes are written to the audit log; the device list and the next 5651 lookups use them at once.
vlans.vlanIdHint: 1–4094; empty for a network without one (e.g. transit)
vlans.subnetHint: Network address and prefix length, e.g. 10.0.20.0/24
vlans.subnetEditHint: Correcting the network keeps the VLAN's name, department and flag; devices are matched against the new network.
vlans.dhcpServerHint: Its name on the router, e.g. dhcp20; empty for a static network
vlans.departmentHint: The department of devices without a person
vlans.guestHint: A guest network that leaves through another exit than the FortiGate (e.g. a separate line, a VPN tunnel): 5651 results say there are no FortiGate records, only DHCP/ARP.

confirmDelete.title: Delete the VLAN
confirmDelete.body: Delete {{vlan}} ({{subnet}}, {{name}})? Devices in this network lose the VLAN name and the VLAN's department, also on the usage pages. Raw logs, leases and stored 5651 results do not change; the usage of the hours without a lease is recomputed by itself for the recent days.

errors.subnet: This is not a network address; e.g. 10.0.20.0/24 or fd00:0:0:20::/64.
errors.hostBits: The host bits must be zero: the network address is {{network}}.
errors.hostBitsNoNetwork: The host bits must be zero: enter the network's first address.
errors.vlanId: A VLAN id is a whole number from 1 to 4094 (or empty).
errors.dhcpServer: A DHCP server name has no spaces or colons, e.g. dhcp20.
errors.ipv4Mapped: This is an IPv4 network written as IPv6; enter the IPv4 network: {{network}}.

export.title: Export (CSV)
export.description: The whole lists; for a filtered list use “Download CSV” on the Devices and Persons tabs. Opens in Excel (UTF-8, separated by ;, times in local time, evet/hayır for yes/no). The file holds personal data: keep it only as long as needed and do not pass it on. Every export is written to the audit log.
export.failed: The list could not be downloaded
export.allHint: Downloads the whole list as a CSV file (holds personal data).
export.filteredHint: Downloads every page of the filtered list as a CSV file (holds personal data).

import.title: Import (CSV)
import.description: The file is checked first and applied when you confirm. UTF-8, separated by ; or ,; at most {{size}} and {{rows}} rows.

persons.title: Persons
persons.description: A line with the id column of an exported list updates that person (also one without an employee number); a line without an id but with an employee number updates the person with that number (or adds one); a line with neither adds a new person. An exported person list imports unchanged. The usage_excluded column (evet/hayır) is optional: a person marked evet is not shown as a person in usage reports; an empty cell changes nothing.

assignments.title: Device assignments
assignments.description: Each line assigns a MAC address to a person, found by the employee number or, without one, by an exact and unique name. The file never adds devices and assigns none to inactive persons.

import.checkFailed: The file could not be checked
import.cancelled: The re-authentication was cancelled; nothing was changed.
import.dryRunNote: This was a dry run: nothing has been written yet.
import.refusedNote: The records changed after the check and some lines are refused now; nothing was written. Correct the lines and check the file again.
import.doneNote: The changes were saved and written to the audit log.
import.errorsBody: Correct these lines and check the file again; an import with refused lines is not applied.
import.confirmBody: {{created}} records will be added and {{updated}} updated. The changes are written to the audit log.

usage.description: Internet usage by company, department, person, device, site and category. Durations are estimated from connection logs.
usage.method_note: Estimated value: computed from connection logs; tabs left open in the background may count too.
usage.methodFooter: Durations are computed in 1-minute slices and are not exact screen time; time per site splits each minute by its traffic, raw time counts every minute in which the site was active.
usage.anonymousHint: Pseudonym: with this setting your role cannot see the names of persons and devices.
usage.loadFailed: The usage data could not be loaded
usage.capped: Showing the {{shown}} with the most time of {{total}}; the exported file has all of them.

hours.label: Hours

computed.none: The usage data has not been computed yet

hints.activeUsers: Persons and devices with active minutes

hints.noActivity: No active minutes in this period

departments.personsHint: The department's persons with every metric

form.recipientsHint: Type an address and press Enter; you can also paste a comma-separated list.
form.personLevelHint: A table and a detail section for every employee with activity (with names).
form.pseudonymizeHint: Off by default; when on, the report shows pseudonyms such as Kullanıcı-7F3A instead of names.
form.enabledHint: When off, the report does not run on schedule; it can still be run by hand.

recipients.duplicate: This address is already in the list.

validation.time: Write the time as HH:mm, e.g. 07:15.
validation.endOfDayMidnight: An end-of-day report cannot run at 00:00 (its period would be empty). Choose a time from 00:01 to 23:59, or the kind “Full day” for the whole previous day.
validation.recipientsForEnabled: An enabled report needs at least one recipient.
validation.periodOrder: The end must be after the start.
validation.periodFuture: The end must not be in the future.
validation.periodTooLong: A period covers at most 92 days.

run.title: Run now
run.send_one: E-mail it to the recipient ({{count}} address)
run.send_other: E-mail it to the recipients ({{count}} addresses)
run.sendHint: When not ticked the report is only created; its files can be downloaded from the run history.
run.noRecipients: This schedule has no recipients: the report is only created.

preview.title: Preview: {{name}}
preview.description: The preview is neither stored nor sent to anyone.
preview.pdf: Open the PDF in a new tab

runs.title: Run history
runs.caption: Report runs, newest first

delete.title: Delete the schedule?

file.title: Licence file

timeSources.vault_day: newest sealed day in the vault

errors.tooLarge: The licence file is too large (at most 64 KiB).

missing.title: The administration service is not running
missing.body: The administration service (ArciAdmin) is not responding; server settings cannot be saved from the browser now. The values are shown read-only. Start the "ARCILOGGER Yönetim" service on the server.

disabled.title: Browser administration is switched off
disabled.body: Browser administration is switched off on this installation; the values are shown read-only.

restart.title: A change waits for a restart
restart.body: arcilogger.toml was changed by hand on the server; that change takes effect only when the service concerned is restarted.

progress.waitingForAgent: The administration service has not answered yet; it may be stopped. The request waits until it expires.

progress.heldUntil: This change is held: it is applied at {{time}} ({{left}} left). It can be cancelled until then.
progress.held: This change is held; it is applied when the hold ends.
progress.active: Applied: the services run with the new settings.
progress.partiallyActive: Partly applied: the configuration was written, but not everything has taken it.
progress.notReloaded: {{service}} has not loaded the new settings yet.
